To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
academic staff recruitment processes are becoming increasingly standardized, but at different pace and to a different extent, depending on national and local contexts.

(a) recruitment processes are being standardized, (b) the degree and pace of standardization is different for different countries and institutional types, (c) the degree of standardization is higher for the more prestigious disciplines, and (d) the degree of convergence in recruitment processes is lower for the less prestigious disciplines.
the recruitment processes of academic personnel are increasingly standardized, but that there is still a great diversity in the way they are implemented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of academic labour markets and the ways in which academic staff is recruited.
the question of how academic recruitment is changing in the context of the Bologna Process, and the implications for academic careers.
the dynamics of the academic profession in a globalizing higher education system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the academic profession has not yet been globalized, but it has certainly been internationalized.
the global model is not yet fully established in academic recruitment practices.
there is a general trend toward convergence in recruitment processes, but this is not a uniform process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recruitment of academic staff is being increasingly standardised in Europe, although at different pace and with different outcomes.
academic careers have become more standardized, but that this standardization is not uniform and does not affect all academic careers in a uniform way.

the global model of academic recruitment is not a reality yet, but that there are strong pressures for convergence, which are however not equally present and strong across the different national and local contexts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global models of recruitment are not being adopted in a similar way by all countries.
the global model of academic career is being constructed by the interplay between the global and the local.

academic recruitment practices are becoming globalized and standardized, but they are also being shaped by disciplinary fields, institutional and national contexts, which produce variation in the opportunities for academics to move and in the constraints they face in doing so.
